principles: Make the error impossible, not merely caught: the tool executes the pinned command and derives the result, so a false command cannot be authored.
The proof unit is (command, selector): the selector (a string that must appear in captured output) is what distinguishes intents sharing one command.
No unguarded bypass: every write entry point (single and batch) reaches the identical enforcement boundary via one shared helper.
Immutable pin without PLAN foreknowledge: pin on the first evidence write and freeze thereafter, since the implementation does not exist at PLAN.
Don't hard-break in flight: grandfather existing prose-only evidence behind an explicit, attributable, gate-visible escape.
drivers: The defect is an interface defect (no command/selector on the intent, intentRef-equality is the only binding), so the fix must be at the interface, not in discipline.
16/19 burn rows shared one command; only a free-text case name distinguished them — a bare expectedCommand field would not have caught F-045/F-061.
All machinery exists (executor, receipt shape, allowlist), so reuse beats reinvention.
manual|docs cannot execute, so an un-demoted attestation path would be a trivial escape hatch around the whole mechanism.
B-3b88 owns refresh_stale, so the write path (add/batch_add) is the only surface this story may harden.

options.name: A: Execute-and-stamp in the write handlers; pin on the intent; shared helper; gate demotes manual/docs
pros: A false pass is impossible for executable intents — the tool runs the command and derives result/receipt
The selector-in-output check kills F-045/F-049/F-050/F-061 directly
One shared helper guarantees single + batch parity (closes the batch bypass both reviewers flagged)
Reuses the existing executor + receipt shape + allowlist
Pin-on-first-write needs no PLAN foreknowledge and freezes drift
cons: Touches the intent-freeze logic (must allow ADD-verification while forbidding change)
Coverage gate must learn executed-receipt vs attestation (manual/docs demotion) — a behavior change other gates read
Executing a command inside an evidence write adds latency and an allowlist/timeout surface

options.name: B: Add a bare expectedCommand string field and validate equality (no execution)
cons: Still trusts caller result:pass — a lie about the outcome survives
Would not catch F-045/F-061 (same command, wrong/absent case) — the burn proved a bare command field insufficient
No receipt, so reviewers still read prose numbers

options.name: C: Ship only a separate verification_run command now; leave add/batch_add trusting the caller
pros: Clean new command; no change to existing handlers
cons: The trusted add-path stays open — the floor is exactly the add-path, so this defers the actual fix
verification_run is the ergonomics layer (follow-on ①b), not the enforcement floor

chosen: A: Execute-and-stamp in the write handlers; pin on the intent; shared helper; gate demotes manual/docs
rationale: Only Option A moves the enforcement to the interface and makes a false pass impossible rather than discouraged, and it is the enforcement FLOOR the program spec names as Step 2's core. B is insufficient (proven by the burn: a bare command field misses the case-name confusions and still trusts result). C defers the real fix to the ergonomics layer and leaves both write paths trusting the caller. A reuses the existing executor/receipt/allowlist, and a single shared enforce-and-stamp helper closes the batch bypass both INIT reviewers flagged. The two accepted costs — a controlled exception to the intent freeze (ADD-only pin) and teaching the coverage gate to distinguish executed receipts from attestation — are exactly what makes the mechanism sound, and both are covered by the RED-first smoke.

preMortem.scenario: verification_evidence_add is guarded but verification_evidence_batch_add is left trusting the caller, so evidence still gets in via the batch path.
preMortem.trigger: The implementer factors the enforcement into verification_evidence_add only; batch_add has independent construction and is easy to miss.
preMortem.consequence: The whole mechanism is bypassable — the exact defect, just via a second door; both INIT reviewers pre-flagged this.
preMortem.mitigation: One shared enforce-and-stamp helper called by BOTH handlers; the CHK-006 smoke asserts a selector-absent row is refused through the BATCH path too; plan.md CHK-002 DoneWhen requires both entry points routed through the same helper.

preMortem.scenario: manual|docs stays attestation but the coverage gate keeps scoring it equal to an executed receipt, so an automatable intent is recorded as type:manual to skip execution.
preMortem.trigger: buildVerificationCoverage treats any result==='pass' as covered; the demotion is added to the handler but not to the gate.
preMortem.consequence: type:manual becomes a universal escape hatch and the mechanism is voluntary.
preMortem.mitigation: Demote in the coverage function itself (verification.ts): an executable intent (logic|cli|browser) is only 'covered' by an executed receipt; a manual/docs attestation is marked non-mechanical and cannot cover an executable intent. Smoke asserts a manual attestation does NOT satisfy an executable intent's coverage.

preMortem.scenario: The pin-on-first-write mutation collides with the intent freeze — either it is rejected (can't pin at all past DEV) or it is allowed too loosely (the pin can be changed later, defeating immutability).
preMortem.trigger: verificationIntentProtectedPhases blocks the write, or the ADD-verification exception also permits overwrite.
preMortem.consequence: Either evidence can never be recorded for executable intents in DEV+ (hard break), or the pin is mutable and drift returns.
preMortem.mitigation: A narrow, explicit exception: the evidence-write path may SET verification only when absent, never change it; a second write with a different command/selector is refused with receipt-command-mismatch. Smoke covers: first write pins; second write with a different command refused; second write with the same command re-executes and passes.

preMortem.scenario: The migration hard-breaks in-flight stories that already have prose-only evidence with no pinned (command,selector), stranding them mid-lifecycle.
preMortem.trigger: The new refuse-on-missing-pin fires on legacy evidence written before this story.
preMortem.consequence: Every active story with prior prose-only evidence cannot advance until manually repaired — a repo-wide stall.
preMortem.mitigation: Grandfather: legacy evidence rows without a pin remain valid (flagged non-mechanical); the execute-and-refuse enforcement applies to NEW writes for executable intents. Provide an explicit, attributable, gate-visible escape (policy mode / audited repair). Smoke loads a legacy evidence row (no verification pin) and asserts it still reads without throwing.
